Absorb an unowned divide into its neighbour instead of deleting it

Source: R/absorb_orphan_divides.R
dot-absorb_orphan_divides.Rd

When a divide's flowpath is swapped away or cleared, that divide is left unowned. Deleting it removes its polygon from the layer, and with it that land's coverage: on a single CONUS VPU this cost 97 km2, invisible because divides_area_conserved compares sums at a 0.5% tolerance and a hole and an overlap removal look alike in a sum.

Usage

.absorb_orphan_divides(div, orphans_mask)

Arguments

div

Divides sf.

orphans_mask

Logical vector over div rows marking unowned divides.

Value

A list with div (the repaired layer), n_absorbed and n_kept (orphans that found no neighbour and were retained).

Details

Unowned is not the same as empty. The land still drains somewhere, so the polygon is merged into the neighbouring divide it shares the most boundary with, which conserves coverage while keeping one divide per flowpath. A divide with no neighbour at all is kept rather than dropped, since losing area is worse than carrying an unowned polygon forward.
